top_module.name: sram_mbist_demo_controller
top_module.description: Top-level SRAM scratchpad controller with internal register map, software-accessible memory operations, BIST request/status handling, and a child SRAM wrapper instance named u_sram.
top_module.functionality: Implements a small scratchpad controller with a register-set style local management interface. It accepts write/read strobes and addresses for controller registers, exposes memory write/read programming fields, latches BIST control/status, and generates an interrupt when enabled and BIST completion or failure is latched. The controller instantiates the memory wrapper as u_sram and uses the wrapper's single functional access path to reach the 256x32 SRAM. The top-level outputs reflect controller readiness, BIST outcome, and interrupt status for firmware and DFT validation.
responsibilities: Decode the external write/read strobes and local register addresses.
Maintain control, status, memory address, memory write-data, memory read-data, BIST control, BIST status, and IRQ status state.
Drive the SRAM wrapper interface through one functional access path.
Expose software-visible read data from register and memory readback paths.
Provide explicit BIST request and status signaling for downstream MBIST collateral generation.
Assert irq only when IRQ_ENABLE is set and a BIST completion or failure status is latched.
top_module.reset_behavior: On reset, the controller clears CONTROL, STATUS, MEM_ADDR, MEM_WDATA, MEM_RDATA, MEM_CONTROL, BIST_CONTROL, BIST_STATUS, IRQ_STATUS, ready, bist_done, bist_fail, irq, and any internal busy or pending state. The memory wrapper is held in a safe deselected state during reset.
behavior_rules: CONTROL bit 0 enables controller operation, bit 1 requests a soft reset, and bit 2 enables irq generation.
STATUS reports ready, bist_done, bist_fail, and busy state.
MEM_ADDR holds the 8-bit SRAM address.
MEM_WDATA holds 32-bit write data to be written into the SRAM.
MEM_RDATA is read-only and captures the most recent SRAM read data.
MEM_CONTROL bit 0 requests a memory write and bit 1 requests a memory read.
BIST_CONTROL bit 0 starts a BIST request from bist_start or software, and bit 1 clears latched BIST result state.
BIST_STATUS reports done, fail, running, and last_fail_addr[7:0].
IRQ_STATUS latches bist_done and bist_fail events until cleared by IRQ_CLEAR.
irq asserts when IRQ_ENABLE is set and either BIST_DONE or BIST_FAIL is latched.
The SRAM wrapper instance name must remain u_sram and must present clk, csb, web, addr, din, and dout ports to preserve macro detectability.
The wrapper may bind to the qualified Sky130 macro or to the synthesizable fallback model, but the controller interface must not change.
The controller must remain synthesizable and avoid vendor-only primitives in the fallback path.

modules.name: demo_sram_32x256_wrapper
modules.description: Functional scratchpad wrapper that exposes the canonical SRAM access interface and binds to the qualified Sky130 SRAM macro when available or to the synthesizable fallback model when collateral is unavailable.
modules.functionality: Provides the single functional access path to a 256x32 scratchpad memory. The wrapper preserves the macro-compatible signal naming expected by downstream synthesis and MBIST tools. Its implementation contract is to map these canonical ports directly onto the prebuilt Sky130 SRAM macro when present, otherwise onto a synthesizable memory model with identical behavior and port naming. The wrapper exists to keep the memory intent explicit and to isolate controller logic from implementation details.
responsibilities: Preserve exact SRAM macro-compatible port naming and directionality.
Expose a single functional memory access path for the controller.
Allow binding to the prebuilt SRAM macro or the fallback model without changing upstream controller behavior.
Keep memory intent discoverable for synthesis, DFT, and MBIST collateral generation.
modules.reset_behavior: The wrapper itself does not hold architectural state beyond the bound memory implementation; on reset, the underlying memory path must be held deselected through csb and web so that no unintended write occurs.
behavior_rules: csb is active-low chip select.
web is active-low write enable.
When csb is deasserted, memory access is inactive and dout may hold its previous value or a macro-defined quiescent value.
The wrapper maintains the exact same interface whether it binds to the macro or the fallback model.
The wrapper must not expose additional control ports that would obscure the canonical memory interface.

modules.name: demo_sram_32x256_model
modules.description: Synthesizable fallback memory model for the same 256x32 scratchpad interface used by the wrapper when macro collateral is not available.
modules.functionality: Implements a simple synthesizable 256-word by 32-bit memory with the same canonical clk, csb, web, addr, din, and dout interface as the wrapper contract. The model exists only as fallback collateral for simulation and synthesis when the qualified prebuilt macro is unavailable. It must preserve functional semantics so downstream tools can later replace or wrap the path with the real macro and MBIST instrumentation without interface changes.
responsibilities: Provide a synthesizable stand-in for the memory wrapper contract.
Maintain exact width and addressing behavior for a 256x32 scratchpad.
Preserve macro-compatible access semantics for AutoMBIST and integration tooling.
modules.reset_behavior: The model initializes to a safe, deterministic state under reset behavior defined by the integration wrapper; memory contents may be left unspecified unless the implementation chooses a known reset fill for simulation convenience.
behavior_rules: The memory depth is 256 words and each word is 32 bits wide.
Addressing is byte-addressed in the narrow 8-bit memory address space of the wrapper contract.
Writes occur only when csb is asserted and web indicates a write operation.
Reads occur only when csb is asserted and web indicates a read operation.
The model interface must remain interchangeable with the wrapper contract for tooling that detects the SRAM macro path.

top_level_connections.description: Top clock drives the controller and the child memory wrapper.
Top reset is consumed by the controller itself.
Top write enable is consumed by the controller control path.
Top write address is consumed by the controller register path.
Top write data is consumed by the controller register path.
Top read enable is consumed by the controller register path.
Top read address is consumed by the controller register path.
Top BIST request input is consumed by the controller BIST request path.
Controller drives the top read data output.
Controller drives the top ready status output.
Controller drives the top BIST done status output.
Controller drives the top BIST fail status output.
Controller drives the top interrupt output.

inter_module_signals.name: sram_csb
inter_module_signals.description: Chip select from controller to the memory wrapper.

inter_module_signals.name: sram_web
inter_module_signals.description: Write enable from controller to the memory wrapper.

inter_module_signals.name: sram_addr
inter_module_signals.description: Memory address from controller to the memory wrapper.

inter_module_signals.name: sram_din
inter_module_signals.description: Memory write data from controller to the memory wrapper.

inter_module_signals.name: sram_dout
inter_module_signals.description: Memory read data from the wrapper back into controller readback state.
